# nsys lean profile (2026-09-06) — Generated by Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic)

## Finding
The "minimal" profile of the v5/split campaigns (`nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --export=sqlite
--cuda-event-trace=true`) never disabled CPU sampling and context-switch tracing. The Nsight
Systems user guide (CLI profile switches): `--sample` and `--cpuctxsw` default to `process-tree`
whenever nsys launches a target. Evidence in a split run (apriltag nsys_1, nsys 2025.6.3):

| sqlite table | rows | consumed by the model |
|---|---|---|
| SAMPLING_CALLCHAINS | 1 894 916 | no |
| SCHED_EVENTS | 332 412 | no |
| NVTX_EVENTS | 321 415 | no (ingested only) |
| CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_CUDA_EVENT | 4 335 | no |
| CUPTI RUNTIME / KERNEL / MEMCPY / MEMSET / SYNCHRONIZATION | 26k / 12k / 2k / 2k / 5k | yes |

The model reads exactly RUNTIME, KERNEL, MEMCPY, MEMSET, SYNCHRONIZATION (ingest_pg.py,
gpu_attribution.py, gpu_dag.py). CPU sampling (perf NMI + callchain unwinding in-process) and the
scheduler trace are in-process costs — consistent with the nsys overhead being independent of the
observer placement (tensor_rt −16 % v5 / −19 % split; bi3d_freespace −12 / −14 %).

## New base flags (python/fish/nsys_flags.py, both wrapping paths)
nsys profile --trace=cuda --sample=none --cpuctxsw=none --backtrace=none --cudabacktrace=none
  --cuda-memory-usage=false --cuda-um-cpu-page-faults=false --cuda-um-gpu-page-faults=false
  --cuda-event-trace=false --cuda-graph-trace=graph --cuda-trace-all-apis=false
  --gpu-metrics-devices=none --stats=false --export=sqlite --force-overwrite=true
Validated on nsys 2025.6.3 in fish-r2b-apriltag-wip and autoware-dev-trt-a1000-fishwait10 (report +
sqlite generated). Opt-ins: FISH_NSYS_NVTX, FISH_NSYS_SAMPLE (v5-style), FISH_CUDA_EVENT_TRACE,
FISH_CUDA_GRAPH_NODE, FISH_CUDA_TRACE_ALL_APIS. overhead_sweep_v4.sh CUDA_EVT default 1 → 0;
run_overhead_modes.sh nsys mode no longer sets FISH_CUDA_EVENT_TRACE=1; fish_settings.ini
cuda_event_trace = false.
